# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–37 (Updated 2026-10-13, Final Revision 3)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: Spring of tenth year after Waterloo (1831). Story spans from Sunday, 26th April dinner (Chapters 1–35) through Chapter 36 (winter into summer) to Chapter 37 (spring). Emperor of China dinner scheduled Monday, 8th July; election for Westminster borough Tuesday, 9th July (three weeks ahead as of Chapter 35). Chapter 37 set in Harrowgate (hill farms including Mirecombe), market towns (Bryngate, Salwick), and London.
- **Key Locations**: London (Welbeck Street, Grosvenor Square, Abchurch Lane, Beargarden Club, Bruton Street, Queen's Gate, Islington, City Road Music-Hall); Coventry Island; Queen's Crawley; Southend; Harrowgate; coastal towns (Lowestoft, Penzance, Brighton, Salwick); rural areas (Sheep's Acre Farm, Staveton, Bryngate, Beccles, Caversham, Pickering).

## Major Deaths
John Sedley, Mr. Osborne, Joseph Sedley, Colonel Rawdon Crawley, Sir Pitt, Wevie Lindner (died winter, buried Salmere).

## Rebecca's Arc
Never became Lady Crawley; styles herself so. Son (Sir Rawdon) receives allowance but refuses to see her. Appears wealthy at Bath/Cheltenham, busies herself with piety and Charity Lists.

## Amelia and William Dobbin
Married at Ostend; Amelia initiated encounter. Dobbin quit service, rented "the Evergreens" (Hampshire). Devoted father; daughter Jane his pride.

## Lady Carbury and Family

**Lady Carbury**: Welbeck Street resident with Felix and Henrietta. Authored "Criminal Queens." Crushed by "Evening Pulpit" review; praised by "Morning Breakfast Table" (Mr. Broune). Rejected Mr. Broune's proposal via letter by six o'clock evening, sent via Didon to Pall Mall East. Full of regrets; in debt. Chapter 36: Attended soirée with Roger Carbury; found Paul and Henrietta together upon return. Disbelieved accidental visit claim. Cross-examined Henrietta on intentions. Allowed Henrietta to leave after kissing. **Chapter 37: Expressed wonder at Alf (editor of "Evening Pulpit"), noting he has sailed "within the wind" but now risks three or four thousand pounds in legal expenses by attempting to prove something (nature unspecified).**

**Felix Carbury**: Beautiful; cynosure of mother's eyes. Won £2,000 from Lord Grasslough, £400 from Miles Grendall at gaming. Director of South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway. Won £200 cheque from Melmotte if withdrew from Marie. **Chapter 37: Amenable to elopement with Marie Thursday week from Liverpool noon. Didon "very urgent" he recover funds to Melmotte. Frequently at City Road Music-Hall. When Ruby pressed marriage demand, refused outright: "Marry, Ruby! No, I don't ever mean to marry. It's the greatest bore out." Deemed such a lie beneath his baronetcy. Plans New York departure as escape. Now resolved on elopement despite written promise to Melmotte; anticipates quarrel "thoroughly internecine" upon discovery. Visited Melmotte in city; received £200 cheque (not full amount promised); departed seeking to recover more funds through other means.**

**Henrietta Carbury**: Rejected Roger's suit (too young, age disparity). Paul returned "as still dear friend" within week, promising not to see her three months. Wore rose from Roger's room. Roger declared love anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination unshaken. Paul thoroughly in love with her. Chapter 36: Paul visited her at Welbeck Street in Lady Carbury's absence. Told mother she loves someone else and praises Roger as "rock of strength" who "never lies."

## Ruby Ruggles
Granddaughter of Daniel Ruggles (Sheep's Acre). Pretty with long glossy ringlets. **Chapter 37: Working as servant/maid to Mrs. Pipkin (her aunt) at Islington who lets lodgings with five children. Very fond of dancing, perhaps liked it better than anything. Danced with Felix at City Road Music-Hall. When Felix refused marriage demand, Roger Carbury visited her at Mrs. Pipkin's house. Ruby disclosed her grandfather Daniel Ruggles had pulled her by hair when undressed, nearly getting into bed—witnessed by Sally Hockett. She fled for protection. Roger warned Felix "is as bad as bad can be...would ruin you and cast you from him without a pang." Praised John Crumb as noble, loving, wanting only her happiness and respectability. Ruby found conviction borne upon her though struggling against it, viewing Crumb's nobility as "dusty, mealy, and also...dumb." Roger warned if Felix and John Crumb were alone together, something would happen to Felix. Extracted promise she would not see Felix again. His words weakened her admiration for Felix.**

**John Crumb**: Country lover from Suffolk, "Bungay mealman." Chapter 35: After supper, moved to take Ruby's hand; Ruby fled. Rode to Carbury Hall searching for her. **Chapter 37: Daniel Ruggles describes him as "regular enough" if Ruby let him; "like clockwork—only the slowest clock out." Roger views him as noble, loving, gallant; capable of forgiving everything if Ruby returns, but will "see the matter out" if she does not, persisting in slow fashion of his own.**

**Daniel Ruggles**: Holds Sheep's Acre Farm on bishop's lease; Roger Carbury's tenant. **Chapter 37: Violent under gin and water; pulled Ruby by hair when undressed (witnessed by Sally Hockett). Told Roger "whoever it is ought to speak out his mind"; says "a girl has to mind herself."**

## The Melmottes

**Augustus Melmotte**: Chairman, South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Company. Big man with large whiskers; expression of mental power on harsh vulgar face. Rumours of gigantic swindler. Candidate for Westminster parliament seat. Planning Emperor of China dinner (8th July, Monday) and Westminster election (9th July, Tuesday). Chapter 36: Called Paul to Grosvenor Square, offered Paul £6,000 to accept and leave or go abroad. **Chapter 37: Received visits from Sir Felix and Paul in city. Extremely busy with electioneering speeches, Committee members, dinner orders, and gigantic commercial affairs. Told Felix: only entitled to shares for £600 now, will see it put right. To Paul, proposed Mexican embassy: "if you'll say when you're ready to start, we'll draw up something of instructions...The chief thing will be a cheque for the expenses; eh? We must get that passed at the next Board." Referenced instructions, Fisker's involvement, managing from Pekin. Paul found tone dubious; reference to expenses disgusted him. Melmotte expressed relief dinner would be over, noting "It's a deal easier to make a treaty with an Emperor, than to give him a dinner."**

**Marie Melmotte**: Speaks English well; forming own opinions. Rejected Lord Grasslough. **Chapter 37: Elopement plan with Felix confirmed: Travel to Liverpool Thursday week, board S.S. "Adriatic" at noon bound for New York. Marry on board or at New York. Return within month to force father's acceptance. Didon to pose as aunt; Felix as "Smith"; Marie as French girl. Had key to Grosvenor Square gardens; Didon to unlock gate. Marie obtained £200; awaits Felix's recovery of more funds.** Engaged to Lord Nidderdale (Chapter 35).

## The Longestaffes

**Sir Merton Longestaffe**: Determined no London expenses; family will not return from Caversham. Desires to sell Pickering and disembarrass Caversham from debt. Dolly refused consent unless half produce given to him.

**Adolphus (Dolly) Longestaffe**: Has rooms in Bruton Street. **Chapter 37: Idle, foolish, dissipated, generally indifferent to debts, but likes what belongs to him. Arrangement made: £5,000 pay off all tradesmen's debts, leave him comfortably possessed; other £20,000 make his property free. Charm in this awakened even Dolly, almost reconciled him to father's society. Went to Caversham, made his own terms; father unable to move him. Returned to father early morning (about two o'clock) enquiring about money. Had not yet received single ten-pound note from sale. Demanded cheque upon Melmotte's bank payable to his own: "A cheque upon his bank which I can pay in to mine is about the best thing going." Instructed father to tell Melmotte; threatened to employ Mr. Squercum (lawyer, odious to father) if money not paid quickly. Father knew son; quite sure Squercum would have finger in pie unless money paid quickly. When Dolly took idea into his head, no power on earth could turn him.**

**Georgiana Longestaffe**: Made protest against Melmottes. Following morning received invitation to stay with them. By Sunday, present at Grosvenor Square.

## South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Scheme

**The Enterprise**: Railway from Salt Lake City, branching from San Francisco/Chicago line, through New Mexico/Arizona into Mexico, terminating Vera Cruz. Approximately 2,000 miles. Stock at par; shares sold at premium "to run them up even to 110." Directors understood fortune made by floating shares, not building railway.

**London Directorate**: Melmotte (chairman), Lord Alfred Grendall, Sir Felix Carbury, Samuel Cohenlupe (MP for Staines), Lord Nidderdale, Paul Montague.

## Paul Montague and Mrs. Winifrid Hurtle

**Paul's Situation**: Living at Beargarden. Junior railway firm member. Dislikes Fisker. Trembles for his money. Thoroughly in love with Hetta. **Chapter 37: Visited Mrs. Hurtle at Islington evening. She received warmly, explained recent absence to Southend with Mrs. Pipkin and baby (Harrowgate air "muggy"). Urged him pursue Mexican railway; offered accompany as companion. Paul tacitly admitted if journey made, she might be traveller. Mrs. Hurtle, leaning forward, asked: "Must the purpose be told to-night?" Expressed weakness, cowardice; solitude during last weeks; begged: "if it be cruel, or harsh, or painful...then drop your purpose for to-night." Eyes showed "only love." Suggested travel to "little place that would be pretty" for health. Paul suggested Brighton (rejected), Penzance (rejected), Orkney (rejected), Lowestoft (accepted with delight). Requested Paul take her to Lowestoft: "It is desolate for a woman to go into such a place all alone." Paul's face troubled, brow black, endeavouring to think. Mrs. Hurtle pressed: "I don't think you will let me ask in vain for such a favour as that." Paul suggested Saturday, 29th; must attend next Board and promised to see Melmotte before Board day. Mrs. Hurtle agreed. Asked if she should meet him at railway station; he undertook to fetch her. As he took leave, she stood close, put cheek up for kiss. Paul took her in arms and kissed her lips and cheeks. Departure resolved nothing; confession deferred.**

Later, waiting in Melmotte's outer room, Paul remembered whence Carbury must have heard tidings of Mrs. Hurtle: through Ruby Ruggles. When rumour was mentioned to him (nature unspecified), Paul declared: "Then you've been told an infernal falsehood" and warned: "I don't know who can have told you, but if you hear it again, I'll trouble you to contradict it."

**Mrs. Winifrid Hurtle**: Formerly betrothed to Paul. Arrived Wednesday. During earlier engagement promised to follow him; renewed promises in New York. Theatre evening: Paul took her. Does not like Frenchmen; prefers Englishmen to Americans. Thinks he should marry her or world hear story of his perjury. Most fond of baby, like Mrs. Pipkin. Now unwell, weak and cowardly; eyes show only love. Wants travel to Lowestoft for health. Paul to fetch her; visit scheduled Saturday, 29th.

## Lord Nidderdale
Intent on marrying Marie for fortune. Engaged to Marie (Chapter 35).

## Mr. Broune
Editor, "Morning Breakfast Table." Nearer fifty than sixty; young of his age. Chapter 35: Proposed to Lady Carbury. When he read her rejection letter: stood at fireplace, left letter on table. Felt admiration greater than ever.

## Roger Carbury
Nearly forty. Never owed shilling he couldn't pay. Firmly opposed Melmotte connection on principle. Works as priest on day-labourer's wages. Soft heart; knows Lady Carbury false and Felix worthless. Declared love to Henrietta anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination unshaken. **Chapter 37: Visited Ruby at Islington; warned her forcefully against Felix; praised John Crumb's nobility and love; extracted promise she would not see Felix again. Spoke to Mrs. Pipkin about Ruby's late hours.**

## Minor Characters
**Lord Alfred Grendall**: Elder Grendall. **Chapter 37: Nearly overwhelmed by electioneering; declared willingness to help Melmotte but nearly in rebellion: "If this goes on much longer I shall cut it." Burdened with seating arrangements for dinner; doesn't know rank precedence (director of bank vs. book-writer); relies on Herald's office fellow.**

**Miles Grendall**: Secretary to Melmotte. Does not pay debts of honour. Suggested father consult Herald's office fellow about rank matters.

**Didon**: Marie's attendant; facilitates elopement plan; to receive £50 before boarding ship. "Very urgent" with Felix to recover funds to Melmotte.

**Father John Barham**: Priest, Beccles.

**Mrs. Pipkin**: Ruby's aunt at Islington; lets lodgings with five children. Most fond of baby. Roger spoke to her about Ruby's late hours.

**Sally Hockett**: Witnessed Daniel Ruggles pulling Ruby by hair.

**Mr. Squercum**: Lawyer employed by Dolly; odious to Sir Merton. Threatened employment if Dolly's money not paid quickly.

**Ulvie Hollwood (also Ulvie Hollmere)**: Gave birth to son named Jonar Hollmere; father Fetho Hollmere. Family lived in Salwick.

**Chapter 37 Provincial Vignettes**: Neena Brackwood, Dalde Brackwood, Pebin Wexwood, Breena, Orric, Lutho, Jonar Hollmere, Fetho Hollmere, Jonar (duplicate), Lutho Hollmere, Aewyn, Orvie Hollett, Daric Brackwood, Lubin, Rorine, Isnar Brackwood. Atmospheric details: clouds, rain wrongly predicted then holding off, muddy squares, light going early, vespers bell, coins counted twice (short one penny), ribbons bought and regretted, almanac mispronounced, torn sleeves mended, river up in spring, chalk sun on forge wall, ruts and puddles after thaw, smoke lying flat, bees humming in lavender, dog barking then quiet, letters sorted by candlelight, children chasing hoop, cart with turnips.
